ORAL ORDER
The petitioners, who are facing trial for offences punishable under Section 498A of the IPC, have approached this Court challenging the order passed by the Trial Court.
The order in question pertains to the application filed under Section 91 of the Cr.PC, which was confirmed by the learned Sessions Judge.

2. The de facto complainant filed a complaint alleging that while she was in her matrimonial home,
accused No.1 (her husband), accused No.2 (her father-in-law), and accused No.3 (her sister-in-law)
subjected her to both mental and physical cruelty.

The petitioners subsequently filed an application seeking to summon the complainant's medical records from Apollo Hospital, Chennai, asserting that there was no specific allegation against accused Nos.1 to 3.
However, their application was rejected.

The petitioners contended that, during her examination-in-chief, PW1 produced a discharge summary issued by Apollo Hospital, Chennai, as evidence that she had received treatment for injuries allegedly caused by the accused.
After hearing the learned counsel for both parties, it is evident that the discharge summary was marked as Ex.P5.

The petitioners argued that Ex.P5 was issued following the guidelines of the competent authority and that the complainant's original complaint contained no allegations that accused No.1 had assaulted her, necessitating medical treatment in Chennai.

They further alleged Dr. Arun K vs State By Bellandur Police Station on 6 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189219126/
2 that the document was fabricated and, accordingly, filed an application under Section 91 of the Cr.PC to summon the original medical records from Apollo Hospital, Chennai.

sentences.text: 4. A perusal of the medical document indicates that there is no reference to an assault by accused No.1 while the complainant was in her matrimonial home.
Furthermore, there is no mention of her traveling to Chennai for treatment as a result of such an assault.
Additionally, the complainant has filed a petition in OP No.4201/2021 seeking the dissolution of her marriage with accused No.1.

In those proceedings, she produced a discharge summary allegedly issued by Apollo Hospital, Chennai,
which consists of four pages.
However, Ex.P5, as produced in the present case, contains only one page.

Notably, the name and address of the hospital are not visible on Ex.P5.
5.
The petitioners assert that summoning the original medical records is necessary to establish that the complainant has produced a fabricated discharge summary solely to falsely implicate the accused.
The requested documents are crucial to ensuring a fair trial, as guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

Given these circumstances, the petitioners NC: 2025:KHC:9629 have established a prima facie case for summoning the documents sought in their application under Section 91 of the Cr.PC.
6.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed.

The impugned order dated 17.01.2023, passed on the application in CC No.16089/2018 by the learned 41st Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate,
Bangalore City, is hereby quashed.
